original:
Let $m\geq 2$ , and consider a sequence of $2m$ elements of $\mathcal{P}$ with sum zero
in $C_{m}^{5}$ . Let $\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{9}$ be the multiplicities of
 $P_{1},\dots,P_{9}$ divided by $m$ . Then either every $\mu_{i}$ is an integer, or
 $(\mu_{i})$ equals $1/2$ on one of the sets

 $\{P_{1},P_{2},P_{4},P_{5}\},\qquad\{P_{1},P_{3},P_{7},P_{8}\},\qquad\{P_{4},P_{6},P_{7},P_{9}\}$ 

and vanishes elsewhere. Consequently:

(1) 

if $m$ is odd, a sequence of $2m$ elements of $\mathcal{P}$ has sum zero in
 $C_{m}^{5}$ if and only if it consists of $2m$ copies of one element or of $m$ 
copies each of two elements;

(2) 

for every $m\geq 2$ , the same holds for sequences of $2m$ elements of
 $\mathcal{P}^{\prime}=\mathcal{P}\setminus\{P_{1},P_{7}\}$ .
